clue.text: Allow no entry to wicked fellow who's from West Indian island?

parts.note: to bar someone is to refuse them entry
wicked means bad
Ian is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A villain is turned away at the border of a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is a West Indian island, and a native of it is described with this demonym.

clue.text: A boast? Get away!

parts.note: a vaunt is a boast or brag

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a braggart with a scornful exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation ordering someone to leave, equivalent to begone.

clue.text: Sign of growth? Then obtain financial allowance

parts.note: a bud on a plant is a sign of growth
obtain means get

explanation.surface: Seeing growth, someone hopes to secure a bigger spending allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is the sum of money set aside or allowed for spending.

clue.text: Expand appointment to drink one litre

indicators.note: something that drinks takes liquid in, so these letters go inside the appointment word

parts.note: a date is an appointment
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone meeting for a date downs a litre and swells up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or enlarge, as pupils do in the dark.

clue.text: Town to surrender when leader's been got rid of

indicators.text: when leader's been got rid of
indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which here is dropped from the surrender word

parts.note: to hand over is to surrender

explanation.surface: A town capitulates once its leader has been deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: HANDOVER loses its first letter H. ANDOVER is a market town in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Andover is a market town in Hampshire, England.

clue.text: A worker finally snapped with anger: 'Financial exploitation!'

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word worker

parts.note: snapped, as a dog does, means bit
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A worker finally loses their temper and denounces money-market profiteering.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrage is profiting from price differences between markets, a kind of exploitation of finance.

clue.text: Good person said to have spoken hesitantly

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person
said means uttered

explanation.surface: A virtuous person is reported to have spoken haltingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stutter is to speak with hesitations and repeated sounds.

clue.text: The fellow without guile can become cruel

parts.note: he refers to a fellow
artless means guileless, innocent

explanation.surface: An innocent man may yet turn cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartless means without compassion, i.e. cruel.

clue.text: Put down some words about hospital and feel acute embarrassment

indicators.note: about means the writing word goes around the hospital letter

parts.note: to put words down on paper is to write

explanation.surface: Writing about a hospital stay makes someone squirm with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to squirm, as one does from acute embarrassment or pain.

clue.text: Sort of electoral success that may threaten those living on the edge

definitions.text: that may threaten those living on the edge
definitions.meaning: a fall of earth and rock from a cliff or hillside endangers houses at its edge

explanation.surface: An election rout and a geological hazard for clifftop dwellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a crushing election win and a collapse of land down a slope.

clue.text: Very cold bird losing its tail

indicators.note: a word's tail is its last letter, which the bird word drops

parts.note: the bittern is a heron-like marsh bird

explanation.surface: A bird in freezing weather loses its tail feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter weather is extremely cold.

clue.text: Inducement I have to get in money first

parts.note: taken as written
a cent is a coin, money
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone must be paid up front before they will do anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is only a link; the money word is the coin worth a hundredth of a dollar or euro.
explanation.definitionFit: An incentive is something that motivates or encourages action, an inducement.

clue.text: Soldiers coming to wood, a testing experience

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Troops march into a forest for a gruelling exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or difficult trial.

clue.text: Air created by female American actors

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A tune composed by American actresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a programme is to broadcast it.

clue.text: Sounds the h's like the 'yo, ho, ho' robbers?

parts.note: as means like
pirates traditionally sing yo-ho-ho in stories

explanation.surface: Asks whether singing pirates pronounce their aitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yo, ho, ho' is full of breathy h sounds, which fits the picture nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspirate a letter is to pronounce it with breath, as with the h sound.

clue.text: It's right having exceptional performer joining the directors

parts.note: a star is an outstanding performer
the board is a company's directors

explanation.surface: A celebrity joins a company's board, which is said to be the right move.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right-hand side of a ship facing forward.

clue.text: Dull day, rainy at both ends

indicators.note: both ends means the first and last letters of rainy are taken

explanation.surface: A dreary, wet day.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry speech or writing is dull and uninteresting.

clue.text: Combative person who has been honoured in tribe

definitions.text: Combative person who has been honoured
definitions.meaning: in judo and karate a ... is a graded expert in martial arts
One of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.definitionFit: A dan is both a black-belt grade holder and an Israelite tribe.

clue.text: Gossip when salary goes up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: salary means pay

explanation.surface: People chatter when wages rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to chatter or gossip idly.

clue.text: Somewhere of archaeological significance is place in list

indicators.note: in means the place word goes inside the list word

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
to set is to place

explanation.surface: A famous dig site appears on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosetta in Egypt is where the Rosetta Stone was found.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosetta is the Egyptian town where the stone that unlocked hieroglyphs was found.

clue.text: Folk going to the bank hoping to make net gains?

definitions.text: Folk going to the bank hoping to make net gains?

parts.words: Folk going to the bank hoping to make net gains?
parts.note: the bank is a riverbank and the net is a keepnet for catches, not money or profit

explanation.surface: Savers heading to the bank in hope of profit.
explanation.definitionFit: People fishing sit on riverbanks hoping to fill their keepnets.

clue.text: Face the wrong way and sleep

indicators.note: facing the wrong way means the word is turned round

parts.note: pan is slang for a face

explanation.surface: Turning away to take a sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a brief doze or catnap, especially during the day, is a short spell of sleep.

clue.text: A hit, something in verse that's in fashion

parts.note: to lam is to beat or hit
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A hit poem becomes fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: From French, the phrase means in the current style.

clue.text: Place with birds keeping quiet but not very! There's a buzz here!

indicators.note: keeping means the quiet letter is put into the birds' place
but not means the very letter is taken out

parts.note: an aviary houses birds
P is piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: An aviary that keeps fairly quiet, though something hums.
explanation.definitionFit: An apiary is where bees are kept, so it is full of buzzing.

clue.text: Some devilish sir got up as a monster

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top
some means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: A devilish knight rises like a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogrish means like an ogre, the monster of fairy tales.

clue.text: A section of football, i.e. division in league

indicators.note: A section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Talk of football divisions and leagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means joined together in alliance, in league.

clue.text: Grumbles from family women about nothing

indicators.note: about means the family women go around the nothing letter

parts.note: grans are grandmothers, women of the family
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: The older women of the family complain about nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Groans are complaints or grumbles.

clue.text: Noble Agra, strange Indian place

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: Agra is noble, a strange Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now Bengaluru, is a major city in southern India.

clue.text: Coloured rod, trick for catching fish

indicators.note: catching means the trick word goes around the fish word

parts.note: a con is a trick
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A coloured fishing rod used to trick a catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax or chalk for drawing.

clue.text: Religious type in party skirt attending first half of dance

parts.note: a do is a party
a mini is a short skirt

indicators.note: first half means the opening part of the dance word is taken

parts.note: the cancan is a high-kicking dance

explanation.surface: A churchgoer at a party in a short skirt doing a high-kicking dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a friar of the order founded by St Dominic.

clue.text: Guides animals on the farm

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both directs and young bullocks raised for beef.

clue.text: The most I'd drunk as one who used never to drink!

definitions.text: one who used never to drink!

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are tipsy, jumbled up

explanation.surface: A tipsy confession from someone who once was teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: Early Methodists were famous for promoting temperance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Methodist movement traditionally urged abstinence from alcohol.
